Subject: Launch readiness: Operational acceptance test (OAT) checklist + network verification

Hi all,

Per our go/no-go cadence this week I like to kick off the Operational Acceptance Test (OAT) for the Acme private deployment. Attached is the latest runbook (redwood_oat_runbook_v3.pdf), the net-change summary from the infra team (net-change-summary.xlsx), and the network routing diagram we will validate.

High-level plan (today  pre-launch window):
- 09:30-10:30 PDT: network connectivity checks (VPN + BGP routes)
- 10:30-11:00 PDT: firewall/NAT traversal / MTU validation
- 11:00-11:30 PDT: smoke API test (tokenized requests, pinned model checks)
- 11:30-12:30 PDT: telemetry + audit log delivery verification (KMS/S3)
- 13:00-14:00 PDT: failover exercise (region fallback, model variant fallback)

Acceptance criteria (pre-launch):
- All infra nodes reachable from Acme test network, no packet loss > 0.5%
- BGP adjacencies stable, routes announced match net-change-summary.xlsx
- P95 API response for small generation payloads < 150ms under test load
- Audit logs delivered to S3 within 2 minutes of event, encrypted with customer KMS key
- Runbook steps 4.1-4.8 executed without manual escalations

Could Tara confirm Acme's network validation window and provide the VPN test credentials you mentioned in the kickoff? Dev/Vivek/Laura: can you confirm your availability for the slots above and that the preflight scan has been run (attach preflight output if available)?

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_oat_runbook_v3.pdf (PDF), net-change-summary.xlsx (XLSX), network-routing-diagram.png (PNG)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, Tara Singh <tara.singh@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: Operational acceptance test (OAT) checklist + network verification - OAT results

Team,

Summary of OAT (completed 2026-08-02): all critical acceptance criteria met. High-level findings below; full log and artifacts attached (oat-results-summary.pdf).

Network / Connectivity:
- BGP: all expected prefixes from Acme announced and present on our edge routers; no route flaps observed during 60m observation window.
- MTU: previously reported MTU mismatch resolved; verified with 1500/9000 frame sweeps, no fragmentation for our test payloads.
- Firewall: policies for 443, 8200, and 9090 validated; no dropped packets for test flows.

Platform / Functional:
- API smoke: 250 sequential small-generation requests (10 tokens) completed with P95=128ms, median=82ms. One model fallback occurred (pinned model v1.3.2 -> v1.3.1) for 2 requests during a transient GPU worker restart; automated fallback worked and no errors propagated to client.
- Telemetry & audit logs: delivery to customer S3 validated; KMS-encryption verified using key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01; average delivery latency 36s.
- Health checks: all nodes returned healthy (GCP-private + on-prem pool) under 5m load ramp.

Operational notes / follow-ups:
- Action: create runbook step to permanently fix MTU on acme-cgw-2 (JIRA-OPS-1427) — Dev please pick up this week.
- Action: schedule a 30-day audit replay to ensure log retention pipeline is stable (owner: Vivek).
- Action: add the fallback incident to the post-mortem if the underlying GPU failure recurs.

Recommendation: Accept for launch. I like to proceed with cutover window tomorrow morning 08:00 PDT, with a 60-minute monitoring hold and immediate rollback criteria in runbook section 9.

LGTM from SRE and Networking. Tara, please confirm if Acme is ready to flip DNS records at 08:00 PDT tomorrow per the runbook.

Thanks everyone — excellent coordination.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment: oat-results-summary.pdf (PDF)
